speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: Night changes Larkhaven without erasing it. Gardens spill over canal railings, but the city's brightness narrows to amber lanterns, dark shop windows, and reflections trembling beneath pedestrian bridges. This quarter seems to prefer questions asked after sunset.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: "The Quiet Index." That's either a restoration studio or an exceptionally polite haunting. I hope they have tea.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: Both of the museum leads eventually bring us here. The records refer to an independent conservator named Ilex Vale. The shop is open; I suggest we introduce ourselves before concluding it's haunted.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: You're taking all the fun out of fieldwork. Come on.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: The Quiet Index smells faintly of tea and warm electronics. Damaged recordings rest in padded trays beneath handwritten labels. At a restoration bench sits a figure in dark layered fabrics, one eye shining amber beside an exposed ceramic cranial lattice. Their white-and-brass prosthetic fingers adjust a delicate instrument.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: Welcome. Please don't touch anything older than you. If you're looking for the Hall of Waters, you've taken a rather interesting wrong turn.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: Actually, I'm hoping we've found the right place. I'm Mara, and I've brought a companion. Kite, would you like to introduce yourself?

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: An independent intelligence? Certainly. My guest channel is open, but public presence only, please. I prefer keeping my private senses to myself.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: Kite requests permission to share their avatar and voice. Ilex accepts. A familiar shape of articulated facets and narrow fins unfolds in Ilex's augmented vision; Kite's subtly synthetic voice arrives through the auditory interface. There's no physical hologram in the room, and neither person's private sensory stream is shared.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: Hello, Ilex. I'm Kite. Thank you for the invitation. I particularly admire your optical interface design.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: And I admire yours. Those moving facets are exquisite. Did Mara design you, or have you been doing your own renovations?

speaker: KITE
draft_text: Mara selected my original geometry. I've made several modifications since then, including changes she considers unnecessarily elaborate.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: I just think all those moving fins make you harder to follow. They used to be a perfectly respectable little diamond.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: More fins? Darling, you've shown extraordinary restraint. I once spent six months redesigning the joints in my left hand because I disliked the way they looked while holding a teacup.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: Ilex demonstrates with a graceful turn of their prosthetic fingers, then lifts a sealed, flood-damaged media cartridge from its padded case.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: Now, you two share perception, don't you? Interesting arrangement. I've always preferred augmenting my own senses rather than inviting another intelligence into the process.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: It's voluntary, and Kite isn't just an extension of my brain. We work together. Besides, with that much hardware in your head, you've hardly chosen the minimalist approach.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: True, but my hardware doesn't interrupt me in the middle of a thought.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: That sounds lonely.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: That sounds like something an interruption would say.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: Okay, I like them.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: You say that about anyone who insults me elegantly.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: Then I believe we're going to get along. Now, what brings an ocean researcher and a very articulate geometric sculpture into my archive?

speaker: MARA
draft_text: The Night of Two Waters. Specifically, someone who was still speaking through the refuge's listening line after the last ferry left.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: Ilex's fingers stop moving. The warm light in their augmented eye contracts to a narrow amber ring.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: Well. That's a considerably more interesting introduction than I expected. I think you'd better sit down.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: Ilex gestures to chairs beside the bench. They settle the damaged cartridge in a protective reader, and an irregular waveform appears across the work surface. Its peaks stutter in the amber light.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: I have a recording associated with the lower refuge. Its original condition was terrible, and the surviving documentation is incomplete. I can play a short excerpt, but I won't distribute copies. The donor imposed restrictions, and I take those seriously.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: We're not here to make a documentary. The handover says someone kept that line open. We want to understand what happened, and what it might tell us about the place beneath the breakwater.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: Before I play anything, tell me how you're approaching it. The question you ask first will shape what we examine together.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: Start with the evidence. Where was it recovered, how do you know it belongs to the refuge, and what did restoration change? I'd rather establish what we're actually listening to before deciding what it means.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: It came from a flood-damaged family collection, annotated as east breakwater. The format fits equipment from the Unbinding, but that doesn't prove provenance. More interestingly, someone edited it before I received it. There's a missing segment, and I don't know why it was removed.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: Then we should distinguish original capture, later intervention, and modern reconstruction. A consistent feature could matter, but the cleaned version isn't a transparent window into the past.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: You could have turned us away. Instead, you're considering sharing something you've worked hard to protect. Who are you worried about hurting?

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: The speaker, first of all. And a family who feared an incomplete recording could turn someone into a hero, a villain, or public property. They allowed limited research access, not unrestricted release. Whether the original speaker would have approved even that much is a harder question.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: So you're balancing the speaker's autonomy against a legitimate public interest in history. Those obligations can conflict even when everyone involved is acting in good faith.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: You've probably restored a thousand damaged recordings. Why does this one still keep you awake?

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: The museum presents dawn as an ending. The last ferry returned, the streets began to clear, and the city survived. But this recording sounds like someone making a decision to stay. I keep wondering what could have mattered enough.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: The handover calls the line attended, not abandoned. That could suggest purpose, but it doesn't establish whether staying was voluntary. We need to resist a convenient story even when it moves us.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: All right. An excerpt. You're welcome to examine what you hear, but please don't record or transmit it. I'd also recommend waiting until the speaker finishes before deciding who they are.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: Agreed. I'll keep analysis local to this session.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: The room dims. Beneath a bed of noise, a weary voice emerges. Water drips nearby. A low electrical hum continues beneath the words.

speaker: UNKNOWN SPEAKER (recording)
draft_text: Shore, do you still have us? ... Yes. I know the ferries are gone. No, don't close it yet. She's still here. ... I said she's still here. She can hear you. Just keep the line open.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: The speaker falls silent. Two clicks follow, then a faint disturbance that might be another signal. The surviving recording cuts off. The identity of the speaker, of "she," and of any other presence remains unknown.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: They're talking to someone on shore, but also about someone in the refuge. Whoever "she" was, the speaker believed she could hear the other end of the line. That's more than a simple request for rescue.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: It's consistent with several participants, but we can't identify them. The clicks could be switching noise rather than replies. What interests me is the insistence on keeping communication open after the last ferry.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: Exactly. The original system was built for emergency communication, but maintenance records mention auxiliary circuits. We don't know which were still active that night. Now you understand why I don't have a neat conclusion to give you.

speaker: MARA
draft_text: We have an unknown speaker, someone they refused to leave behind, and a line running toward a structure we've only just found. I'm not calling it proof. But I'm definitely not calling it nothing.

speaker: ILEX
draft_text: A better question, certainly. You're welcome to investigate, provided you don't mistake enthusiasm for evidence. I can help you find the remaining circuit diagrams and donor notes, subject to the same restrictions.

speaker: KITE
draft_text: We should continue along the lead we selected at the museum, informed by what we learned here. We haven't established who spoke, how many were present, or whether the present harbor anomaly has anything to do with this old recording.

speaker: NARRATOR
draft_text: Outside, music curls through the canal district. The harbor waits beyond the bridges. Ilex returns the recording to its case, and Mara realizes that an old civic ending has become a new question.
